build-and-check.text: Build the documentation with Nix. The documentation check validates rendered links, anchors, speech and theme assets. Separate model and simulator checks exercise the proved Lean model and finite corpus, and the model check cross-checks the compiled axiom report against the theorem manifest; no application proof is claimed. The browser check launches pinned Chromium and executes actual simulator controls using a temporary local server. The build gate realizes packages, checks, and development shell inputs before downstream jobs.

generated-api-references.text: The site ships a generated reference for each library a contributor calls into, built from the same revision as the pages that link it: Haddock for the off-chain library's public modules and for the Conformance library, and the pinned Aiken docs output for the registry validators.

The six package-private node owners, the executables and test suites, and the separate naming validators have no generated reference by decision; their owner pages link each source file, and the private library's ledger and provider types are documented where the public library re-exports them.
Each generated reference carries a manifest binding its pages to the digests of their source, and the documentation check fails when a page, its source or its link targets no longer agree.

the-repository-code-inventory.text: The repository code inventory command maps every file the tree holds to a lint policy and a format policy, or to a named non-code class, and fails on anything unmapped. Discovery walks the tree through extensions, shebangs, executable mode and component manifests, so a new source file in a covered directory is mapped automatically while a file nobody classified fails with a named diagnostic. The same inventory runs over the Nix flake source, where no Git directory exists, and pull request CI runs both forms so the contexts cannot drift. The inventory is a mapping, not enforcement: the report names the CI carrier that executes each policy, and every lint and format policy is enforced, with no code family left unchecked and no source directory excluded. A controls command injects synthetic orphans into scratch copies of the classified tree, each required to produce its intended failure, and never touches the working tree.

haskell-formatting.text: The Haskell trees are formatted with Fourmolu under one house configuration, fourmolu yaml at the repository root. Every formatter entrypoint passes that file explicitly, so a missing configuration fails loudly instead of falling back to Fourmolu defaults, and there is no per-tree configuration to drift from it. Run just format to apply it to every discovered Haskell source and just format-check for the same check the CI carries; discovery covers both trees with no directory exclusions, the formerly fenced verifier sources and the evaluation spike included. The Conformance tree gets the same check in its own Nix source context through the format-check app. The format controls run over scratch copies: a source Fourmolu defaults accept but the house configuration rejects must fail the check, its formatter correction must pass it again, and a tree without the configuration must fail loudly. HLint runs over the same discovered extent with no exclusions and no ignore file, in the off-chain lint app and in the Conformance lint app beside its format check.

other-languages.text: Every other code family the inventory discovers is linted and format-checked by one command, just lint, over the inventory's own extent, with the tools the development shell pins: nixfmt, statix and deadnix for Nix; ruff for Python; shfmt and shellcheck for shell; Biome for JavaScript and CSS; the just formatter for justfiles; yamlfmt and actionlint for workflow YAML. Lean and HTML have no general formatter here, so explicit style rules are the policy: no tab, no carriage return, no trailing whitespace, and exactly one final newline. Aiken sources are checked by aiken fmt inside the two on-chain flake checks, and formatting leaves every compiled validator and its hash unchanged. Generated files are regenerated from their formatted sources. The lint controls plant one defect per family in scratch copies and require each check to fail, and a code family nobody checks fails the run instead of passing silently.

edit-and-serve.text: Use the Nix development shell for a strict MkDocs build or live local server. A separate CI build verifies that shell.
The build and serve recipes stage the generated references from the packaged site build, so the local site links the same generated pages CI checks, while the Markdown pages still reload live.

publication-and-accessibility.text: Pull requests have a live preview without comments. Main publishes through GitHub Pages. The site includes a light and dark theme toggle that remembers the choice, and section read-aloud controls using browser voices.

Diagrams are Mermaid, rendered by the copy the shared toolchain pins as a Nix input and served from the site itself, in the selected theme, with a full-size viewer. No page loads a script or stylesheet from outside the site, and the site check fails if one does.

documentation-releases.text: The documentation version is whichever one the version file, the release manifest and the changelog agree on; a prepared version does not establish a tag or a published archive. Release-please proposes later version changes in a pull request. An operator-authorized version tag on its merged commit publishes the Nix-built archive and checksum, verifies uploaded bytes, then updates bookkeeping labels without comments.

The archive is also a runnable review workspace. Under artifacts review it carries model and theorem sources, corpora, scenarios, simulator and replay sources, checkers, and a minimal flake with its exact lock. After extracting the actual archive into a fresh directory, verify the internal checksum manifest and run the review flake's check app. Nix may acquire only the exact locked toolchain; all model and replay inputs come from the archive. A checkout pass or presence check does not establish archive reproduction. Published releases, each produced by this workflow from a tag on main, are listed on the repository's GitHub releases page.
